text: Which caution is specifically raised about codon-optimizing a gene solely to maximize its Codon Adaptation Index (CAI)?
choices: CAI-optimized sequences always increase translation initiation rate (TIR) by an identical amount, regardless of mRNA secondary structure
Maximizing CAI does not necessarily maximize expression, because mRNA secondary structure effects and repeat-sequence-driven recombination instability also matter
Codon optimization has no effect on protein expression, since all synonymous codons are translated at identical rates
CAI can only be calculated for eukaryotic genes and cannot be applied to bacterial genes
explanation: The chapter specifically cautions that maximum CAI does not equal maximum expression, because secondary-structure effects on mRNA folding also influence translation, and introducing repeated sequence elements during optimization can cause recombination instability. Choice 0 overstates CAI's effect and ignores this secondary-structure caveat. Choice 2 is factually wrong -- rare codons cause real effects such as ribosome pausing and queuing, which is precisely why codon choice matters. Choice 3 is a fabricated limitation; CAI applies to genes in any organism with known codon usage tables, including bacteria.
